newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Holderbank - 1997 net to at least match 96.
newsitem.headline: Holderbank - 1997 net to at least match 96.

text.p: Holderbank Financiere Glarus AG, the world's leading cement producer, said it was certain 1997 net profit would at least equal last year's.
"We are convinced that 1997 net profit will least reach the 1996 level," chief executive Thomas Schmidheiny said.
He also said the first quarter was satisfactory, especially in European business, which was badly reduced in the first quarter last year by severe winter weather.
Schmidheiny said his forecast for 1997 full year net profit referred to the level of last year's net profit before a one-time special change taken for restructuring.
Holderbank posted a net profit of 646 million Swiss francs, up 5.7 percent from 1995, but the special charges reduced the figure to 43 million francs.
"Cautious optimism is the right word," Schmidheiny said about his expectations for this year's results.
He said it was too early in the year to be more specific in his forecast, adding that the development of the dollar over the year was one significant factor that would influence the final result.
"In the first quarter we started significantly better in Europe based on better weather than last year," Schmidheiny said.
Europe, excluding Switzerland, accounts for about one-third of Holderbank's sales. Severe winter weather last year depressed construction and cement demand in major European markets.
"Altogether, we have started the year satisfactorily," he said when asked about the group's overall performance in the first quarter. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
